{
  "candidate_rtl": "module pw_fsm_sync (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg done
);

localparam [8:0] S_IDLE  = 9'b000000001;
localparam [8:0] S_START = 9'b000000010;
localparam [8:0] S_READ  = 9'b000000100;
localparam [8:0] S_PROC1 = 9'b000001000;
localparam [8:0] S_PROC2 = 9'b000010000;
localparam [8:0] S_PROC3 = 9'b000100000;
localparam [8:0] S_WAIT  = 9'b001000000;
localparam [8:0] S_DONE  = 9'b010000000;
localparam [8:0] S_ERROR = 9'b100000000;

reg [8:0] state, next_state;

wire idle_s  = (state == S_IDLE);
wire start_s = (state == S_START);
wire read_s  = (state == S_READ);
wire proc1_s = (state == S_PROC1);
wire proc2_s = (state == S_PROC2);
wire proc3_s = (state == S_PROC3);
wire wait_s  = (state == S_WAIT);
wire done_s  = (state == S_DONE);
wire error_s = (state == S_ERROR);
wire valid_s = idle_s | start_s | read_s | proc1_s | proc2_s |
               proc3_s | wait_s | done_s | error_s;
wire read_match = data_in[3] & ~data_in[2] & data_in[1];
wire error_exit = &data_in[2:0];

always @(*) begin
    next_state = 9'b000000000;
    next_state[0] = ~valid_s | (idle_s & ~start) | done_s |
                    (error_s & error_exit);
    next_state[1] = idle_s & start;
    next_state[2] = (start_s & data_in[0]) | (wait_s & data_in[4]);
    next_state[3] = read_s & read_match;
    next_state[4] = proc1_s;
    next_state[5] = proc2_s & data_in[7];
    next_state[6] = (read_s & ~read_match) |
                    (proc2_s & ~data_in[7]) |
                    (wait_s & ~data_in[4]);
    next_state[7] = proc3_s;
    next_state[8] = (start_s & ~data_in[0]) |
                    (error_s & ~error_exit);
end

wire [7:0] incremented;
assign incremented[0] = ~data_in[0];
assign incremented[1] = data_in[1] ^ data_in[0];
assign incremented[2] = data_in[2] ^ (&data_in[1:0]);
assign incremented[3] = data_in[3] ^ (&data_in[2:0]);
assign incremented[4] = data_in[4] ^ (&data_in[3:0]);
assign incremented[5] = data_in[5] ^ (&data_in[4:0]);
assign incremented[6] = data_in[6] ^ (&data_in[5:0]);
assign incremented[7] = data_in[7] ^ (&data_in[6:0]);

wire pass_s = read_s | done_s;
always @(*) begin
    data_out = ({8{pass_s}} & data_in) |
               ({8{proc1_s}} & incremented) |
               ({8{proc2_s}} & {data_in[6:0], 1'b0}) |
               ({8{proc3_s}} & ~data_in) |
               ({8{error_s}} & 8'hEE);
    done = done_s;
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (rst)
        state <= S_IDLE;
    else
        state <= next_state;
end

endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "Likely timing-sensitive cones are state decoding into next-state selection and the PROC1 increment followed by output selection. Actual critical-path attribution requires the specified mapped STA run.",
  "rewrite": "Retain the original state and next_state names and all nine encodings. Express transitions as parallel Boolean equations with shared exact-state decodes. Implement the increment using explicit reduction-prefix carries, and combine mutually exclusive output terms in parallel while sharing the READ/DONE pass-through enable.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The explicit carry reductions expose balanced carry computation rather than requiring inference from an addition operator, while parallel transition equations remove procedural selection structure. These changes target improved setup WNS, but the gain is mapping-dependent and is not measured or guaranteed here.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Shared decodes and the shared pass-through output term may reduce duplicated selection logic. Prefix carry reductions can increase intermediate wiring or logic depending on mapping. Compliance with the 1102.432320um2 area cap, electrical constraints, and timing requirements requires synthesis and physical evaluation.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves ports, synchronous reset priority, clocking, state encodings, combinational output timing, and modulo-256 increment behavior. Exact equality decodes preserve the original invalid-state behavior: every unrecognized state produces zero outputs and transitions to S_IDLE. Thus correctness does not depend on assuming an initially valid one-hot state. No initialization, additional latency, helper modules, latches, assumptions, or undefined outputs are introduced."
}
